crypto_published_justification: https://github.com/blisspixel/recon/blob/main/src/recon_tool/http_backend.py uses httpx.create_ssl_context() and preserves the TLS server name; https://www.python-httpx.org/advanced/ssl/ documents verified HTTPS through Python SSL/OpenSSL. https://github.com/blisspixel/recon/blob/main/src/recon_tool/remote_server.py uses standard-library SHA-256 and hmac.compare_digest for its opt-in bearer adapter; no cryptographic primitives are reimplemented. https://github.com/blisspixel/recon/blob/main/docs/supply-chain.md documents Sigstore verification.
crypto_call_justification: https://github.com/blisspixel/recon/blob/main/src/recon_tool/http_backend.py uses httpx.create_ssl_context() and preserves the TLS server name; https://www.python-httpx.org/advanced/ssl/ documents verified HTTPS through Python SSL/OpenSSL. https://github.com/blisspixel/recon/blob/main/src/recon_tool/remote_server.py uses standard-library SHA-256 and hmac.compare_digest for its opt-in bearer adapter; no cryptographic primitives are reimplemented. https://github.com/blisspixel/recon/blob/main/docs/supply-chain.md documents Sigstore verification.
crypto_floss_justification: https://github.com/blisspixel/recon/blob/main/src/recon_tool/http_backend.py uses httpx.create_ssl_context() and preserves the TLS server name; https://www.python-httpx.org/advanced/ssl/ documents verified HTTPS through Python SSL/OpenSSL. https://github.com/blisspixel/recon/blob/main/src/recon_tool/remote_server.py uses standard-library SHA-256 and hmac.compare_digest for its opt-in bearer adapter; no cryptographic primitives are reimplemented. https://github.com/blisspixel/recon/blob/main/docs/supply-chain.md documents Sigstore verification.
crypto_password_storage_justification: https://github.com/blisspixel/recon/blob/main/src/recon_tool/remote_server.py accepts an operator-provided bearer token for its optional adapter, or delegates ingress authentication to a trusted platform; it has no user-password registration or persistent password database. https://github.com/blisspixel/recon/blob/main/deploy/container/README.md requires a randomly generated token and external secret management. This answer does not claim the remote adapter is unauthenticated.
crypto_random_justification: https://github.com/blisspixel/recon/blob/main/deploy/container/README.md delegates optional bearer-token generation to the operator using Security.Cryptography.RandomNumberGenerator. recon does not generate its own cryptographic keys or nonces; TLS randomness is supplied by Python SSL/OpenSSL, and https://github.com/blisspixel/recon/blob/main/docs/supply-chain.md delegates signing to OIDC/Sigstore.

release_notes_vulns_justification: Review every applicable release against publicly assigned recon runtime advisories; dependency CVEs are outside this criterion. https://github.com/blisspixel/recon/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md and https://github.com/blisspixel/recon/blob/main/docs/security-audit-resolutions.md provide release and fix records, but an empty GitHub advisory list alone does not establish complete coverage.
report_responses_justification: The 2026-10-20 public tracker review found 26 issues, all maintainer-authored and all closed; this is not an external bug-response sample. Review genuine reports in the criterion's 2-12 month window at https://github.com/blisspixel/recon/issues before attesting.
enhancement_responses_justification: The 2026-10-20 public tracker review found only maintainer-authored requests. Review genuine enhancement responses in the criterion's 2-12 month window at https://github.com/blisspixel/recon/issues; do not manufacture outside requests or response history.
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: The maintainer must check all reports received privately during the last six months, including email. https://github.com/blisspixel/recon/blob/main/SECURITY.md sets a 48-hour acknowledgment target; a policy target and an empty public advisory list do not establish actual response times. N/A is permitted only if no vulnerability reports were received.
know_secure_design_justification: On 2026-10-20 the primary maintainer personally attested to understanding secure design principles, including least privilege, fail-closed defaults, complete mediation, limited attack surface and input validation. The dated attestation is recorded at https://github.com/blisspixel/recon/blob/main/docs/openssf-badge-readiness.md#maintainer-attestation-and-response-history . This is a personal attestation, not a conclusion from CI.
know_common_errors_justification: On 2026-10-20 the primary maintainer personally attested to understanding common vulnerability classes and their mitigations relevant to this project. The dated attestation is recorded at https://github.com/blisspixel/recon/blob/main/docs/openssf-badge-readiness.md#maintainer-attestation-and-response-history . This is a personal attestation, not a conclusion from CI.
crypto_keylength_justification: https://github.com/blisspixel/recon/blob/main/src/recon_tool/http_backend.py uses httpx.create_ssl_context() without reducing its security settings. https://www.python-httpx.org/advanced/ssl/ documents the Python default SSL context; https://docs.python.org/3.11/library/ssl.html#ssl.SSLContext documents security level 2 with RSA/DH keys >=2048 bits, ECC >=224 bits and secure AES/ChaCha20 since Python 3.10, below recon's supported Python minimum. https://github.com/blisspixel/recon/blob/main/src/recon_tool/remote_server.py uses SHA-256 for bearer comparison; operator-generated token entropy remains an explicit deployment responsibility.
crypto_working_justification: https://github.com/blisspixel/recon/blob/main/src/recon_tool/http_backend.py retains verified HTTPX/Python TLS defaults, documented at https://docs.python.org/3.11/library/ssl.html#ssl.SSLContext as TLS >=1.2 with secure AES/ChaCha20 and security level 2. https://github.com/blisspixel/recon/blob/main/src/recon_tool/remote_server.py uses SHA-256 and constant-time digest comparison; no MD4, MD5, DES or RC4 is used for project security mechanisms. Custom Python builds and externally terminated remote ingress require operator review.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: https://github.com/blisspixel/recon/blob/main/src/recon_tool/http_backend.py retains the Python secure TLS defaults documented at https://docs.python.org/3.11/library/ssl.html#ssl.SSLContext; https://github.com/blisspixel/recon/blob/main/src/recon_tool/remote_server.py and https://github.com/blisspixel/recon/blob/main/scripts/verify_github_release.py use SHA-256 for authentication digests and artifact integrity. recon does not implement SSH or use SHA-1 as a project security hash. This is a default-configuration answer, not an audit of externally operated ingress or custom runtime builds.
crypto_pfs_justification: https://github.com/blisspixel/recon/blob/main/src/recon_tool/http_backend.py uses the unchanged HTTPX/Python default SSL context. https://docs.python.org/3.11/library/ssl.html#ssl.SSLContext documents forward-secrecy cipher suites since Python 3.10. TLS is delegated to OpenSSL rather than implemented here. This applies to recon's client TLS defaults; the opt-in remote container terminates TLS at separately configured operator ingress, documented in https://github.com/blisspixel/recon/blob/main/deploy/container/README.md.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: Review public vulnerability discovery and release dates against the 60-day medium-or-higher requirement, using https://github.com/blisspixel/recon/blob/main/docs/security-audit-resolutions.md and release history. Current dependency and code scans have no open vulnerability findings, but that does not establish a complete historical or external disclosure inventory.
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: Requires actual report, confirmation and released-fix dates for any critical vulnerabilities. https://github.com/blisspixel/recon/blob/main/SECURITY.md states response targets and https://github.com/blisspixel/recon/blob/main/docs/security-audit-resolutions.md records fixes; neither replaces a complete report-history review.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: The 2026-10-20 GitHub secret-scanning API returned no alerts, and https://github.com/blisspixel/recon/actions/workflows/secrets-scan.yml runs full-history gitleaks. Scanner success does not prove there is no valid credential outside recognized patterns; confirm credential validity and rotation history before attesting. Never test a possible credential against a service.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: The 2026-10-20 paginated GitHub review found no open CodeQL alerts; https://github.com/blisspixel/recon/security/code-scanning records fixes and test-fixture dismissals. Reconcile confirmed medium-or-higher exploitability, discovery and released-fix dates with https://github.com/blisspixel/recon/blob/main/docs/security-audit-resolutions.md before attesting. The three remaining Scorecard process alerts are not CodeQL runtime findings.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: https://github.com/blisspixel/recon/blob/main/docs/adr/0010-evidence-gated-native-acceleration.md keeps the project runtime and universal wheel pure Python; https://github.com/blisspixel/recon/blob/main/pyproject.toml defines no project-owned C/C++/Rust extension. Native dependencies and the interpreter are external components. https://github.com/blisspixel/recon/blob/main/.github/workflows/clusterfuzzlite.yml still runs Python fuzzing with the address sanitizer, but no project-owned memory-unsafe implementation requires this criterion.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: Review confirmed dynamic-analysis findings and their released fixes against https://github.com/blisspixel/recon/blob/main/docs/security-audit-resolutions.md and https://github.com/blisspixel/recon/actions/workflows/clusterfuzzlite.yml . Passing tests and fuzz runs are current evidence, not a complete inventory of past reports; do not infer N/A merely because the current run passes.
